summary: The study investigates the thermal and plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (ALD) of tantalum and titanium oxides using alkylamide precursors PDMA T and TDMA T. The results show that PDMA T is a promising precursor for both thermal and PE-ALD of Ta2O5, while TDMA T exhibits nonideal growth behavior for TiO2. The study also highlights the advantages of PE-ALD in achieving lower leakage current densities and better film quality.
evidence: The results indicate that PE-ALD produced films with lower leakage current densities than thermal ALD for both Ta2O5 and TiO2, even though the same metal precursor was used for each oxide. Additionally, PDMA T was found to be a promising precursor for both thermal and PE-ALD of Ta2O5, while TDMA T has shown nonideal growth with imperfect self-saturation behavior.
